Petroleo Brasileiro SA Reports Strong Quarterly Earnings Amid Robust Production

Petroleo Brasileiro SA, Brazil’s state-controlled oil and gas giant, posted strong quarterly results on Thursday, buoyed by higher crude output and resilient international prices. The company, commonly known as Petrobras, reported a net profit of 47.8 billion reais ($9.7 billion) for the first quarter of 2024, up 12% year-on-year and surpassing analysts’ expectations.

Revenues reached 157.5 billion reais ($31.9 billion), up from 145.2 billion reais a year earlier. The improvement was largely attributed to increased production from the pre-salt fields in the Santos Basin, which accounted for over 75% of total output in the quarter. Average daily production rose to 2.9 million barrels of oil equivalent, a 4% increase compared to the same period last year.

Petrobras CEO Gustavo Silveira said in a statement, “Our performance this quarter reflects the successful execution of our operational strategy, with a continued focus on efficient production and cost discipline. The results reinforce Petrobras’ role as a key driver of Brazil’s energy sector and its commitment to delivering value to shareholders and society.”

The company’s board approved a dividend payment of 2.18 reais per share, maintaining its policy of distributing at least 45% of free cash flow to shareholders. The announcement comes as Petrobras continues to prioritize debt reduction, with net debt falling to $31.2 billion, its lowest level in more than a decade.

Analysts welcomed the results. “Petrobras continues to demonstrate strong fundamentals, with robust cash flows and healthy margins, despite a challenging global environment,” said Mariana Costa, an oil and gas analyst at Siqueira Advisors. “Their focus on pre-salt development is paying off, and the company appears well-positioned to capitalize on any further improvements in oil prices.”

The Brazilian Oil Workers’ Federation (FUP) also noted the results, pointing to the company’s stable employment levels and continued investment in safety and training programs.

Looking ahead, Petrobras reaffirmed its annual production guidance and outlined plans to invest $16 billion in upstream projects this year, particularly in deepwater exploration. The company said it remains committed to its energy transition strategy, with increased investments planned in natural gas and renewable initiatives.
